## `adapters.list`

Inspect static adapter implementation descriptors.

**Authority:** An authenticated, handshaken client; only its policy-projected data is visible.

- Static implementation coverage is not proof of installation, authentication, model access or successful live execution. Consult the support matrix.

### Parameters

[EmptyParams](schemas.md#schema-emptyparams)


### Result

array of [AdapterDescriptor](schemas.md#schema-adapterdescriptor)


### Example

**Request** (after handshake, unless this is the handshake):

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1,
  "method": "adapters.list",
  "params": {}
}
```

**Successful response** (fictional):

```json

  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1,
  "result": [
    {
      "id": "opencode",
      "name": "OpenCode",
      "integration": "local_http",
      "passiveDiscovery": true,
      "metadata": true,
      "textSessions": true,
      "nativeToolApproval": false,
      "cancellation": true,
      "persistentResumption": false,
      "qualification": "See per-operation qualification reports; no account capability implied",

        "Plan and account quota depend on what the native interface reports"

  ]
}
```

<a id="method-apps-revoke"></a>

## `apps.revoke`

Administratively revoke a connected application and its grant.

**Authority:** A separate administrative policy, targeting a client ID returned by apps.list.

- For app-scoped independent grants this removes the reusable app grant and sweeps its live connections. Legacy owner credentials retain per-connection semantics.

<a id="method-connections-probe"></a>

## `connections.probe`

Refresh one permitted connection through its metadata adapter.

**Authority:** The connection must be visible and the host must permit its metadata provider or exact connection.

- The result can be status:cached when evidence is still fresh. Re-read the snapshot for actual field observations.
- A probe may launch an approved client, use its login and contact metadata services. It is not an inference/tool grant.

### Parameters

[ConnectionParams](schemas.md#schema-connectionparams)

| Field | Required | Wire type | Constraints / description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `connectionId` | yes | `string` | — |

Any JSON value (unrestricted schema)

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 12,
  "method": "connections.probe",
  "params": {
    "connectionId": "connection_example"
  }
}
```

**Successful response** (fictional):

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 12,
  "result": {
    "status": "updated",
    "connectionId": "connection_example"
  }
}
```

### Representative failures

| Code | Condition |
|---|---|
| `LOCAL_ACCESS_DENIED` | The client is not authorized for the referenced scope or object. |
| `CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED` | The operation or selected adapter capability is unavailable. |

<a id="method-discovery-refresh"></a>

## `discovery.refresh`

Request an explicit passive inventory reconciliation.

**Authority:** Host-granted passive discovery; no provider metadata or execution consent is implied.

- Only passive is currently supported. Omitting level uses passive; other levels return a typed unsupported error.
- Concurrent refresh callers share the inventory flight. This is not a quota probe or inference request.

### Parameters

[DiscoveryParams](schemas.md#schema-discoveryparams)

| Field | Required | Wire type | Constraints / description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `level` | no | `string` OR `null` | default: `null` |

Additional properties are forbidden by this schema.

### Result

[DiscoveryResult](schemas.md#schema-discoveryresult)

| Field | Required | Wire type | Constraints / description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | yes | [DataMode](schemas.md#schema-datamode) | — |
| `revision` | yes | `string` | — |

This schema permits additional properties; runtime checks can be stricter.

### Example

**Request** (after handshake, unless this is the handshake):

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 14,
  "method": "discovery.refresh",
  "params": {
    "level": "passive"
  }
}
```

<a id="method-discovery-watch"></a>

## `discovery.watch`

Enable or disable permitted local metadata invalidation watching.

**Authority:** Host-granted passive discovery and an existing discovered watch-root set.

- Watching invalidates cached evidence; it does not grant provider probes. Separately host-authorized autonomous lanes may refresh invalidated data.
- Disable with enabled:false. Client close/revocation removes that client watcher.

### Parameters

[DiscoveryWatchParams](schemas.md#schema-discoverywatchparams)

| Field | Required | Wire type | Constraints / description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | yes | `boolean` | — |

Additional properties are forbidden by this schema.

### Result

Any JSON value (unrestricted schema)

**Request** (after handshake, unless this is the handshake):

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 15,
  "method": "discovery.watch",
  "params": {
    "enabled": true
  }
}
```

**Successful response** (fictional):

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 15,
  "result": {
    "watching": true
  }
}
```

| Code | Condition |
|---|---|
| `LOCAL_ACCESS_DENIED` | The client is not authorized for the referenced scope or object. |
| `CONFLICT` | Enable is requested before passive discovery established watch roots. |

<a id="method-events-read"></a>

## `events.read`

Read a bounded page of owned session events.

**Authority:** A negotiated execution driver, an existing host execution grant, and ownership of the referenced session/turn.

- Session after is a decimal sequence string. Runtime tailCursor/hasMore are additional fields beyond the canonical EventPage minimum.
- The inventory scope uses a different cursor and result type; see the [alpha18 inventory contract gap](../integration/api-reference.md#inventory-events-and-contract-gap).

### Parameters

[EventsParams](schemas.md#schema-eventsparams)

| Field | Required | Wire type | Constraints / description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `after` | no | `string` OR `null` | default: `null` |
| `sessionId` | no | `string` OR `null` | default: `null` |

Additional properties are forbidden by this schema.

### Result

[EventPage](schemas.md#schema-eventpage)

| Field | Required | Wire type | Constraints / description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cursor` | yes | `string` | — |
| `events` | yes | array of [Event](schemas.md#schema-event) | — |

This schema permits additional properties; runtime checks can be stricter.

### Example

**Request** (after handshake, unless this is the handshake):

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 16,
  "method": "events.read",
  "params": {
    "sessionId": "session_example",
    "after": "0"
  }
}
```

**Successful response** (fictional):

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 16,
  "result": {
    "events": [
      {
        "sessionId": "session_example",
        "turnId": "turn_example",
        "sequence": "1",
        "timestamp": "2026-10-22T12:00:00.000Z",
        "adapterId": "documentation-fixture",
        "schemaVersion": "1.0",
        "payload": {
          "type": "text_delta",
          "text": "Hello from a synthetic example."
        }
      }
    ],
    "cursor": "1",
    "tailCursor": "1",
    "hasMore": false
  }
}
```

| `INVALID_REQUEST` | The request fails runtime validation. |

<a id="method-events-subscribe"></a>

## `events.subscribe`

Subscribe to owned native-stream events.

**Authority:** A handshaken native-stream transport advertising subscriptions and permission for the underlying events.read query.

- The stdio/local-IPC native stream implements this operation; HTTP uses GET /v1/events for session SSE, not this RPC.
- events.event and events.error notifications carry this subscriptionId. Preserve the processed cursor and unsubscribe explicitly.

[EventsParams](schemas.md#schema-eventsparams)

| Field | Required | Wire type | Constraints / description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `after` | no | `string` OR `null` | default: `null` |
| `sessionId` | no | `string` OR `null` | default: `null` |

Additional properties are forbidden by this schema.

### Result

Any JSON value (unrestricted schema)


### Example

**Request** (after handshake, unless this is the handshake):

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 17,
  "method": "events.subscribe",
  "params": {
    "sessionId": "session_example",
    "after": "0"
  }
}
```

**Successful response** (fictional):

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 17,
  "result": {
    "subscriptionId": "subscription-1"
```

### Representative failures

<a id="method-models-page"></a>

**Authority:** An authenticated, handshaken client; only its policy-projected data is visible.

| `routeId` | no | `string` OR `null` | default: `null` |

| `models` | yes | array of [Model](schemas.md#schema-model) | — |
| `nextCursor` | no | `string` OR `null` | — |
| `revision` | yes | `string` | — |

<a id="method-runtime-handshake"></a>

## `runtime.handshake`

Negotiate protocol, compiled methods, and runtime-level capabilities.

**Authority:** The transport must already establish its trusted caller identity; this grants no new access.

- The example method list is illustrative, not a promise that every runtime advertises the same subset. A method can be advertised and still require a grant.
- Compare protocolVersion separately from runtimeVersion; package alpha versions are not protocol versions.
- The helper may already have host-authorized background inventory before the first snapshot. Handshake itself does not discover anything.

### Parameters

[HandshakeParams](schemas.md#schema-handshakeparams)

| Field | Required | Wire type | Constraints / description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clientName` | no | `string` OR `null` | default: `null` |
| `protocolVersion` | no | `string` OR `null` | default: `null` |

Additional properties are forbidden by this schema.

### Result

[HandshakeResult](schemas.md#schema-handshakeresult)

| Field | Required | Wire type | Constraints / description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `capabilities` | no | array of `string` | default: `[]`; Runtime-level features such as `turn.input.image` or `session.host_mcp`. Model and adapter support is still per selection. |
| `methods` | yes | array of `string` | — |
| `protocolVersion` | yes | `string` | — |
| `runtimeVersion` | yes | `string` | — |

This schema permits additional properties; runtime checks can be stricter.

### Example

**Request** (after handshake, unless this is the handshake):

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 33,
  "method": "runtime.handshake",
  "params": {
    "protocolVersion": "1.0",
    "clientName": "example-metadata-app"
  }
}
```

**Successful response** (fictional):

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 33,
  "result": {
    "protocolVersion": "1.0",
    "runtimeVersion": "0.1.0-alpha.18",
    "methods": [
      "runtime.handshake",
      "runtime.health",
      "snapshot.get",
      "discovery.refresh",
      "connections.list",
      "models.page",
      "runtime.closeClient"
    ],
    "capabilities": []
  }
}
```

### Representative failures

| Code | Condition |
|---|---|
| `PROTOCOL_INCOMPATIBLE` | The requested protocol major or version syntax is incompatible. |
| `CONFLICT` | Stdio receives a second handshake on the same connection. |

| `selection` | yes | [Selection](schemas.md#schema-selection) | — |
| `state` | yes | [SessionState](schemas.md#schema-sessionstate) | — |

Additional properties are forbidden by this schema.

### Example

**Request** (after handshake, unless this is the handshake):

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 40,
  "method": "sessions.resume",
  "params": {
    "resumeToken": "<opaque-resume-token>"
  }
}
```

**Successful response** (fictional):

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 40,
  "result": {
    "id": "session_resumed",
    "connectionId": "connection_example",
    "selection": {
      "routeId": "route_example",
      "modelId": "model_example",
      "revision": "fixture-r1",
      "options": {}
    },
    "state": "ready",
    "createdAt": "2026-10-22T12:00:00.000Z",
    "nativeResumption": true
  }
}
```

### Representative failures

| Code | Condition |
|---|---|
| `RESUME_UNAVAILABLE` | The token, identity, route, model, workspace or native history is no longer valid. |
| `CONFLICT` | The same native conversation is already attached. |
| `LOCAL_ACCESS_DENIED` | The client is not authorized for the referenced scope or object. |
| `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` | The approved provider/runtime cannot complete the operation. |

<a id="method-sessions-suspend"></a>

## `sessions.suspend`

Detach a supported native conversation and obtain a resume token.

**Authority:** A negotiated execution driver, an existing host execution grant, and ownership of the referenced session/turn.

- A token may be helper-lifetime-only. Persistence across helper restart requires the negotiated persistent-resumption capability and a persistent session.
- A failed suspend leaves native state uncertain; do not assume the old session remains safely usable.

### Parameters

[SessionParams](schemas.md#schema-sessionparams)

| Field | Required | Wire type | Constraints / description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sessionId` | yes | `string` | — |

Additional properties are forbidden by this schema.

### Result

[SessionSuspendResult](schemas.md#schema-sessionsuspendresult)

| Field | Required | Wire type | Constraints / description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `resumeToken` | yes | `string` | Opaque, host-storable token. With `session.resume.persistent` it is<br>sealed with a per-install key, carries no credentials, and survives<br>helper restarts; otherwise it lives only as long as the helper. |

Additional properties are forbidden by this schema.

### Example

**Request** (after handshake, unless this is the handshake):

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 41,
  "method": "sessions.suspend",
  "params": {
    "sessionId": "session_example"
  }
}
```

**Successful response** (fictional):

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 41,
  "result": {
    "resumeToken": "<opaque-resume-token>"
  }
}
```

### Representative failures

| Code | Condition |
|---|---|
| `CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED` | The operation or selected adapter capability is unavailable. |
| `CONFLICT` | The session state is not suspendable. |
| `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` | The approved provider/runtime cannot complete the operation. |

<a id="method-sessions-updateoptions"></a>

## `sessions.updateOptions`

Update provider-native session option values.

**Authority:** A negotiated execution driver, an existing host execution grant, and ownership of the referenced session/turn.

- fixture_mode/native_choice_b are fictional descriptors, not universal controls. Use the exact current provider-native descriptor IDs and values.

### Parameters

[SessionOptionsParams](schemas.md#schema-sessionoptionsparams)

| Field | Required | Wire type | Constraints / description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `options` | yes | `object` | — |
| `sessionId` | yes | `string` | — |

Additional properties are forbidden by this schema.

### Result

[Session](schemas.md#schema-session)

| Field | Required | Wire type | Constraints / description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `connectionId` | yes | `string` | — |
| `createdAt` | yes | [Timestamp](schemas.md#schema-timestamp) | — |
| `id` | yes | `string` | — |
| `nativeResumption` | yes | `boolean` | — |
| `selection` | yes | [Selection](schemas.md#schema-selection) | — |
| `state` | yes | [SessionState](schemas.md#schema-sessionstate) | — |

Additional properties are forbidden by this schema.

### Example

**Request** (after handshake, unless this is the handshake):

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 42,
  "method": "sessions.updateOptions",
  "params": {
    "sessionId": "session_example",
    "options": {
      "fixture_mode": "native_choice_b"
    }
  }
}
```

**Successful response** (fictional):

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 42,
  "result": {
    "id": "session_example",
    "connectionId": "connection_example",
    "selection": {
      "routeId": "route_example",
      "modelId": "model_example",
      "revision": "fixture-r1",
      "options": {
        "fixture_mode": "native_choice_b"
      }
    },
    "state": "ready",
    "createdAt": "2026-10-22T12:00:00.000Z",
    "nativeResumption": true
  }
}
```

### Representative failures

| Code | Condition |
|---|---|
| `OPTION_UNSUPPORTED` | The option/value/scope does not match current descriptors. |
| `SELECTION_STALE` | The selection or catalog cursor no longer matches the projected revision. |
| `CONFLICT` | A running or unusable session cannot update options. |

<a id="method-snapshot-get"></a>

## `snapshot.get`

Read the cached, permission-projected inventory.

**Authority:** An authenticated, handshaken client; only its policy-projected data is visible.

- fields is an optional projection of top-level field names. The full Snapshot schema describes an unprojected result; a projection returns only requested keys.
- Reads renew activity interest but do not invoke discovery or widen grants. Previously authorized background lanes can publish concurrently.
- For large catalogs omit models and combine revision-consistent models.page calls; see the [catalog guide](../integration/catalog-pages.md).

### Parameters

[SnapshotParams](schemas.md#schema-snapshotparams)

| Field | Required | Wire type | Constraints / description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fields` | no | array of `string` OR `null` | default: `null` |

Additional properties are forbidden by this schema.

### Result

[Snapshot](schemas.md#schema-snapshot)

| Field | Required | Wire type | Constraints / description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `accounts` | yes | array of [Account](schemas.md#schema-account) | — |
| `connections` | yes | array of [Connection](schemas.md#schema-connection) | — |
| `cursor` | no | `string` | default: `""`; Opaque journal cursor at the committed revision. Subscribe with this<br>value to obtain every inventory change committed after the snapshot. |
| `diagnostics` | yes | array of `string` | — |
| `health` | no | [HealthSummary](schemas.md#schema-healthsummary) | default: `{"hydrated": false, "openIssues": 0, "status": "unknown"}` |
| `installations` | yes | array of [Installation](schemas.md#schema-installation) | — |
| `issues` | no | array of [Issue](schemas.md#schema-issue) | default: `[]` |
| `mode` | yes | [DataMode](schemas.md#schema-datamode) | — |
| `models` | yes | array of [Model](schemas.md#schema-model) | — |
| `observedAt` | yes | [Timestamp](schemas.md#schema-timestamp) | — |
| `profiles` | yes | array of [Profile](schemas.md#schema-profile) | — |
| `protocolVersion` | yes | `string` | — |
| `providers` | yes | array of [Provider](schemas.md#schema-provider) | — |
| `quotaPools` | yes | array of [QuotaPool](schemas.md#schema-quotapool) | — |
| `revision` | yes | `string` | — |
| `routes` | yes | array of [AccessRoute](schemas.md#schema-accessroute) | — |

Additional properties are forbidden by this schema.

### Example

**Request** (after handshake, unless this is the handshake):

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 43,
  "method": "snapshot.get",
  "params": {}
}
```

<a id="method-turns-cancel"></a>

## `turns.cancel`

Request cancellation of a toolkit-owned turn.

**Authority:** A negotiated execution driver, an existing host execution grant, and ownership of the referenced session/turn.

- Cancel is not a refund, rollback, or global process kill. Transport abort alone does not imply this request was accepted.

### Parameters

[TurnParams](schemas.md#schema-turnparams)

| Field | Required | Wire type | Constraints / description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `turnId` | yes | `string` | — |

Additional properties are forbidden by this schema.

### Result

Any JSON value (unrestricted schema)


### Example

**Request** (after handshake, unless this is the handshake):

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 44,
  "method": "turns.cancel",
  "params": {
    "turnId": "turn_example"
  }
}
```

**Successful response** (fictional):

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 44,
  "result": {
    "cancelled": true
  }
}
```

### Representative failures

| Code | Condition |
|---|---|
| `LOCAL_ACCESS_DENIED` | The client is not authorized for the referenced scope or object. |
| `NOT_FOUND` | The turn is unavailable. |
| `TIMEOUT` | The provider did not acknowledge cancellation in time. |

<a id="method-turns-start"></a>

## `turns.start`

Start one explicit model turn in an owned session.

**Authority:** A negotiated execution driver, an existing host execution grant, and ownership of the referenced session/turn.

- This can consume account allowance. The example is documentation only and is never run by the quickstart or docs validation.
- The wire request id, requestId, sessionId and returned turnId are separate identities. Do not automatically replay an ambiguous turn after timeout or reconnect.

### Parameters

[TurnStartParams](schemas.md#schema-turnstartparams)

| Field | Required | Wire type | Constraints / description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `inputs` | no | array of [TurnInputRef](schemas.md#schema-turninputref) | Staged `inputs.put` references. Each input is consumed by the turn that starts with it. |
| `prompt` | yes | `string` | — |
| `requestId` | yes | `string` | — |
| `sessionId` | yes | `string` | — |

Additional properties are forbidden by this schema.

### Result

[TurnStarted](schemas.md#schema-turnstarted)

| Field | Required | Wire type | Constraints / description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `turnId` | yes | `string` | — |

This schema permits additional properties; runtime checks can be stricter.

### Example

**Request** (after handshake, unless this is the handshake):

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 45,
  "method": "turns.start",
  "params": {
    "sessionId": "session_example",
    "requestId": "example-user-action-1",
    "prompt": "This is a fictional example; do not execute it automatically."
  }
}
```

**Successful response** (fictional):

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 45,
  "result": {
    "turnId": "turn_example"
  }
}
```

### Representative failures

| Code | Condition |
|---|---|
| `LOCAL_ACCESS_DENIED` | The client is not authorized for the referenced scope or object. |
| `SELECTION_STALE` | The selection or catalog cursor no longer matches the projected revision. |
| `CONFLICT` | The session is busy or a request identity conflicts. |
| `RATE_LIMITED` | The provider/runtime cannot admit the turn. |
| `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` | The approved provider/runtime cannot complete the operation. |

<a id="method-usage-read"></a>

## `usage.read`

Read visible quota pools and provider usage observations.

**Authority:** An authenticated, handshaken client; only its policy-projected data is visible.

- Unknown is not zero. Pool sharing must be explicitly verified; similar account labels do not establish a shared allowance.
- A reset deadline may schedule another observation but cannot replenish an allowance locally.
